original_question: In the same one-quarter-class setting for orthogonal polynomial sequences, the only known example whose orthogonality measure has spectrum extending over the entire real line is the Meixner polynomials of the second kind (the Meixner-Pollaczek polynomials). Do there exist any other orthogonal polynomial sequences of this type?
target_in_paper: Section 2, unnumbered open question at the end of "Blumenthal–Nevai theorems for the one quarter class of orthogonal polynomials": after defining the one-quarter class and isolating the difficult case σ = -∞, the paper asks whether there are any examples besides the Meixner polynomials of the second kind whose orthogonality measure has spectrum extending over the whole real line.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the correct narrow target in the paper: it stays within the one-quarter class of orthogonal polynomial sequences, identifies the Meixner polynomials of the second kind (Meixner–Pollaczek polynomials) as the only known example mentioned there, and asks the same existence question about further examples.
missing_details: The phrase "same one-quarter-class setting" is not stand-alone; the paper first fixes an OPS by the three-term recurrence P_n(x) = (x - c_n)P_{n-1}(x) - λ_n P_{n-2}(x) for n ≥ 1 with P_{-1}(x) = 0, P_0(x) = 1, c_n real, and λ_n > 0.
The defining asymptotics of the one-quarter class should be stated explicitly: c_n → ∞ and λ_{n+1}/(c_n c_{n+1}) → 1/4.

The paper places the question specifically in the subcase σ = -∞, where σ is defined from limiting zeros: if x_{n,1} < ··· < x_{n,n} are the zeros of P_n, then ξ_i = lim_{n→∞} x_{n,i}, η_j = lim_{n→∞} x_{n,n-j+1}, σ = lim_{i→∞} ξ_i, and τ = lim_{j→∞} η_j; moreover τ = ∞ throughout the one-quarter class.

"Spectrum extending over the entire real line" should be tied to the associated orthogonality measure in the paper’s wording, within the one-quarter-class σ = -∞ discussion, rather than left as a free-floating phrase.

The quantifier should be explicit: the question is whether there exists any other OPS example of this type besides the Meixner polynomials of the second kind; it is not asking for a full classification and not asking the broader preceding question about an analog of Blumenthal’s theorem.
refined_question: Let {P_n}_{n≥0} be an orthogonal polynomial sequence on the real line determined by P_{-1}(x)=0, P_0(x)=1, and, for n≥1, P_n(x)=(x-c_n)P_{n-1}(x)-λ_n P_{n-2}(x), where c_n∈ℝ and λ_n>0. Assume that {P_n} belongs to the one-quarter class, meaning that c_n→∞ and λ_{n+1}/(c_n c_{n+1})→1/4 as n→∞. If x_{n,1}<⋯<x_{n,n} are the zeros of P_n, define ξ_i=lim_{n→∞}x_{n,i}, η_j=lim_{n→∞}x_{n,n-j+1}, σ=lim_{i→∞}ξ_i, and τ=lim_{j→∞}η_j; in this class τ=∞, and the unresolved case singled out in the paper is σ=-∞. Apart from the Meixner polynomials of the second kind (Meixner–Pollaczek polynomials), does there exist any other orthogonal polynomial sequence in this one-quarter class whose orthogonality measure has spectrum extending over the entire real line?
justification: Section 2 is the relevant part of the paper. It first defines the general OPS and the one-quarter-class assumptions, then introduces the limiting-zero parameters σ and τ and notes that τ=∞ in this class. It explains that the remaining difficult case is σ=-∞ and immediately follows that discussion with the more specific existence question about examples: the only known one mentioned is the Meixner polynomials of the second kind, and the paper asks whether any others exist. Your draft is therefore aimed at the correct open problem, but it needs the recurrence, the asymptotic one-quarter-class conditions, and the σ=-∞ context to be fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper’s formulation.
